summary.en: Represent newlines, quotes, backslashes and control characters safely inside C literals.
summary.bn: সি লিটারালের ভেতরে নিউলাইন, কোট, ব্যাকস্ল্যাশ ও নিয়ন্ত্রণ অক্ষর ঠিকভাবে লেখো।

notes: The common escapes in this lesson are available in the C17 baseline and long predate it. C99 added universal character-name facilities for wider character notation, which are separate from the octal and hex byte-value examples here. C23 does not turn terminal-dependent display effects into fixed output guarantees.

examples.title: A two-line marks card
examples.explanationHtml: \t emits a horizontal tab and \n a newline; the raw output contains tabs whose visual width depends on the viewer.

examples.title: Quotes and a backslash
examples.explanationHtml: Escaped double quotes stay inside the string; a doubled source backslash produces one output backslash.

examples.title: A null terminator ends a string
examples.explanationHtml: The embedded zero character ends what %s reads, so Hidden is not printed even though it is in the literal array.

examples.title: Octal and hexadecimal character values
examples.explanationHtml: On this ASCII-compatible host both escape values represent A; numeric character encodings are implementation-dependent.

examples.title: Mistake: an unknown escape
examples.explanationHtml: \q is not a standard escape; the compiler warns. Write \\ in the source for one literal backslash.

quiz.prompt: Which source escape denotes a newline?
quiz.explanation: A backslash followed by n denotes the newline character.
Tab expansion is a display policy; the program emits one tab.
It is an octal escape for value zero, commonly used as a string terminator.

quiz.prompt: Which source spelling produces one backslash inside a string?
quiz.explanation: The first backslash introduces an escape and the second supplies the backslash value.

quiz.prompt: What does \r request on a typical terminal?
options: Return the cursor to the start of the current line
Start the next line by itself
quiz.explanation: Carriage return and newline are different control characters, and rendering depends on the terminal.

quiz.prompt: How many digits can an octal escape consume?
quiz.explanation: An octal escape contains one to three octal digits.

quiz.prompt: Why can "\x41B" surprise an ASCII user expecting A then B?
options: The hex escape consumes B as another hex digit
Hex escapes stop after two digits always
quiz.explanation: Hex escapes consume all following hex digits; split adjacent string literals to end the escape.

quiz.prompt: Where do the tab and newline characters separate the marks-card fields?
quiz.explanation: \t emits a horizontal tab and \n a newline; the raw output contains tabs whose visual width depends on the viewer.

quiz.prompt: Which quotes and single backslash remain after the source escapes are interpreted?
quiz.explanation: Escaped double quotes stay inside the string; a doubled source backslash produces one output backslash.

quiz.prompt: What portion of "Lab\0Hidden" does %s read before reaching null?
quiz.explanation: The embedded zero character ends what %s reads, so Hidden is not printed even though it is in the literal array.

examQuestions.question: Distinguish the null character, the digit zero and the newline escape.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The null character, written as \0 in a literal, has value zero and terminates C strings. The character '0' represents a visible digit and is not that terminator. The escape \n represents a newline for output line separation.

examQuestions.question: Explain octal and hexadecimal escapes and why terminal effects must not be treated as fixed visible output.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
An octal escape consumes one to three octal digits. A hexadecimal escape begins with \x and consumes following hex digits, so split adjacent string literals if a following letter would extend it. Numeric values map to characters according to the execution encoding. Tabs, alerts, carriage returns and backspaces are stream characters whose visible effects depend on the output device; a file can record the byte even without a screen effect.

Marking: octal rule 1, hex consumption 1, split-literal technique 1, encoding 1, rendering distinction 1.

examQuestions.question: Write a complete C program for this lab task: Read roll and marks each 0 to 100; output Input: then "roll" followed by a tab and R, then "marks" followed by a tab and M on separate lines.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int roll, marks;
    printf("Input: ");
    if (scanf("%d %d", &roll, &marks) != 2) {
        return 1;
    }
    printf("\"roll\"\t%d\n\"marks\"\t%d\n", roll, marks);
    return 0;
}

Marking: 1 for typed declarations, 1 for checked input, 2 for the required calculation or transformation, and 1 for exact output.
